entries.title: Psalms 14:1
segments:
, with some variations. 
 
  They are corrupt; the practical atheists menitoned in the preceding words, who feel and act as if there were no God. 
 
The man who wishes that there were no God, or who feels and acts as if there were none, is in the most emphatic sense a fool.

entries.title: Psalms 14:2
segments:
Did understand, and seek God; had any true knowledge of God, or desire for communion with him.  This is to be understood as referring to men's natural state. 
 
The atheism of the heart is the fruitful source of every crime.  They who give themselves up to the practice of sin, banish the thoughts of God; and having done this, have nothing to restrain them from every iniquity.

entries.title: Psalms 14:3
segments:
Not one; that naturally does any thing spiritually good. 
 
All the good that is done or experienced in this apostate world, is the fruit of the grace of God.

entries.title: Psalms 14:4
segments: Eat up my people; plunder and destroy them.

entries.title: Psalms 14:5
segments:
There; in the midst of their wicked oppression of the righteous. 
 
  Were they in great fear; the judgment of God overtook them, and put them in great fear. 
 
Persecutors of God's people often have fearful forebodings of coming wrath.

entries.title: Psalms 14:6
segments:
Shamed; held up to contempt. 
 
Though the poor may be derided for their confidence in God, he will not disappoint them, but in due time will appear to their everlasting joy.

entries.title: Psalms 14:7
segments: Out of Zion; the dwelling-place of God; where he manifested his presence.
